provenance.Extraction_Model_ID: claude-sonnet-5-5 (configured model; calls run in-session, not through the API; the serving model may differ)

study.Analysis_Settings: GMV: SPM12 VBM, images co-registered to the white matter tissue probability map, segmented, study-specific template spatially normalized to MNI space with DARTEL, 8 mm FWHM Gaussian smoothing, intensity threshold 0.2. CT: custom tissue probability map from Template-O-Matic (TOM8), segmentation in CAT12, 10 mm smoothing. Both: 2 x 2 full factorial model, voxel-wise height threshold p < 0.005 uncorrected, cluster-level extent threshold p < 0.05 FDR corrected.
study.Atlas_Parcellation: Brodmann areas and anatomical labels assigned with the label4MRI package
study.Covariates: GMV: total GMV, study site, scanner type, ADHD scores. CT: study site, scanner type, ADHD scores. Age and sex were not included.
study.Multiple_Comparison_Correction: Cluster-level FDR correction at p < 0.05 (voxel-wise height threshold p < 0.005, uncorrected)
study.Pulse_Sequence: T1-weighted; acquisition parameters are not given in the article (referred to the ABCD imaging protocol document)
study.Statistical_Test: 2 x 2 full factorial analysis (ANOVA): main effect of Reading Ability, main effect of Language Background, and their interaction
study.Study_Dataset: ABCD Study, Annual Release 3.0, baseline time point (NDA DOI 10.15154/gx74-8w05)
study.Study_Design_Type: 2 x 2 factorial group comparison (Reading Ability by Language Background) on ABCD baseline data

claims.Claim_Diagnostic_Criteria: NIH Toolbox Oral Reading Recognition Test (TORRT) standard score below 85
claims.Claim_Statement: Children aged 9 to 10 years with reading disability have less gray matter volume in the left cerebellum lobule VI than control children.
claims.Claim_Evidence_Quote: the RD Groups (Bilingual and Monolingual combined) had less GMV than the Control Groups (Bilingual and Monolingual combined) in two regions: (1) left cerebellum lobule VI and (2) right precentral gyrus (BA 6) extending to the superior frontal gyrus (BA 6).
claims.Claim_Population_Qualifiers: ABCD Study; Bilingual and Monolingual groups combined; matched on nonverbal reasoning and socioeconomic status
claims.Claim_Sex_Distribution: RD 71 F, 64 M; controls 71 F, 62 M

claims.Claim_Diagnostic_Criteria: NIH Toolbox Oral Reading Recognition Test (TORRT) standard score below 85
claims.Claim_Statement: Monolingual children aged 9 to 10 years with reading disability have less gray matter volume in the right middle frontal gyrus than monolingual children without reading disability.
claims.Claim_Evidence_Quote: while there was less GMV in Monolinguals with RD relative to Monolinguals without RD in right middle frontal gyrus (t(264) = −3.368, p = 0.005) and middle temporal gyrus (t(264) = −3.2804, p = 0.006), this was not the case for the Bilinguals with and without RD (t(264) = 0.220, p = 0.996; and t(264) = −1.6137, p = 0.373, respectively).
claims.Claim_Population_Qualifiers: ABCD Study; Monolinguals; matched on nonverbal reasoning and socioeconomic status
claims.Claim_Sex_Distribution: Monolingual RD 36 F, 30 M; Monolingual Control 32 F, 33 M
